What it owns is rigour (the structure that keeps a fast-moving engineering team aligned) combined with the technical depth and judgement to apply that rigour credibly in an AI-native, agent-driven environment, and to help others in the TPM function do the same.
This role reports into the Principal Technical Program Manager and partners closely with engineering leads, product managers and client-facing teams. Remote, based in Canada, the US or LATAM, with regular working-hours overlap with our London-based teams.

Key Responsibilities
Tier 1 Client Engineering Requests
• Own the program for engineering requests and requirements coming from our Tier 1 clients: intake, scoping, prioritisation input, sequencing and delivery tracking.

• Partner with client-facing teams, product managers and engineering leads to translate client needs into clear, buildable requirements — and translate engineering reality back to the client side so commitments are realistic.

Operating Rhythm & Cadence

• Apply the minimum viable structure that keeps teams aligned without slowing them down: enough ceremony to make decisions stick, never more.

• Ensure decisions get made on time, with the right people in the room, and with a written trail of what was decided and why.

• Support (not own) the recurring sprint rhythm — planning, standups, retros and demos — and coordinate larger retrospectives across teams when a program or incident calls for one.

Workback Planning & Dependency Management
• Own the workback plans and dependency maps for the programs in your portfolio — releases, integrations, client commitments and cross-team engineering work.

• Hold the full picture for your programs when everyone else is heads-down: what depends on what, who owns what, what is about to slip, and what needs to be escalated.

• Keep your project management tool (e.g. Linear) trustworthy enough that its views can be read without a verbal check: issues correctly labelled, estimated, assigned and in the right state.

• Own the standing views the organisation relies on — production bugs, in-flight work, blocked items, client commitments — so status is a link, not a meeting.

• Actively reduce complexity: automate status collection, reporting and tracker hygiene wherever possible, and lead adoption of new tools and AI-native workflows that make the function faster.

• Surface technical and timeline risk early, challenge optimistic plans, and enforce readiness gates before commitments are made externally.

Cross-Team Program Delivery
• Independently run the programs that require multiple teams to move together — feature launches, client integrations and technical migrations — including those with company-level impact.

• Determine the methods and approach for new or ambiguous programs: scope, sequence and drive them to delivery, owning the schedule, the trade-offs and the comms back to stakeholders.

• Manage the seams between teams — where product hands off to engineering, engineering hands off to another workstream, and client-facing teams hand off to delivery.

• Resolve cross-team blockers directly, going lead-to-lead to clear dependencies so coordination doesn't need to escalate upward.

• Put out fires before they cause harm: spot the program that is drifting and act on it independently.

Risk, Escalation & Decision Support
• Apply and refine the escalation framework: flag what is on track, what is at risk, and what needs a leadership call — and make sure the right call gets made.

• Own the first-responder rota for incidents and client interrupts in your area, absorbing and routing them before they land on a team mid-flow.

• Provide expert advice on complex delivery decisions that affect other teams or the company at large.

• Translate engineering reality for non-technical stakeholders and back again, so no one is surprised by scope or timeline.

• Produce a trustworthy weekly written status for stakeholders and leadership — a one-pager when it's a one-pager moment, a full dependency map when it isn't.

Goal Tracking
• Support engineering and product leads on OKR reporting and tracking: keeping objectives and key results current, surfacing progress and drift each cycle, and turning them into a readable rollup so goal health is visible without a separate chase.

Growing the TPM Function
• Create, not just improve, the templates, cadences and trackers used across the TPM function, and make sure they outlast you.

• Mentor and actively support more junior program managers, and coordinate their activities on shared programs where needed.

• Act as an ambassador for our values in how programs are run and in TPM hiring, including taking part in interview loops.

• Stay current with how leading AI-native engineering organisations run delivery, and bring the best ideas back to Pencil.

Explicitly Not Owned
• People management, performance, growth, and hiring decisions — stay with engineering leadership and team leads.

• Technical decisions and architecture — owned by engineering leadership.

• Priority and product direction — owned by Product Managers.

• The commercial client relationship — owned by client-facing teams; this role owns the engineering delivery behind it.

Your Background
• 8+ years of experience as a Technical Program Manager, ideally in AI/ML, platform infrastructure, or developer tooling.

• Track record independently running complex programs with multi-team dependencies, hard external deadlines and company-level impact.

• Experience owning engineering delivery for enterprise or Tier 1 clients: managing their requests, setting realistic commitments, and keeping them informed without over-promising.

• Experience mentoring other program managers and creating the templates, cadences and norms a young TPM discipline runs on.

• A track record of bringing in new tools or ways of working that measurably reduced overhead for the teams around you.

KPIs & Success Measures
